summary: Hardened vault drift detection by fixing CC#4 (SHA-256 awk had a regex bug that prevented it from ever firing) and CC#5 (cycles/index.md Total cycles regex matched m6/m7/m8 milestone rows, inflating the count by 16). Added CC#54 (bash meta-check, sibling of CC#48) so the 7 bash CCs (CC#1, #4, #5, #6, #46, #53) are now auto-validated alongside the 46 python CCs. refactored check_vault_drift.sh to invoke both meta-checks. Side-effect: 54 stale SHAs in m9-01..m9-10 archive-manifests were detected by the now-functional CC#4 and regenerated.
title: 66 vault drift detection hardening

subject.gap: CC#4 (SHA-256 consistency in archive-manifest Artifact index) had a broken awk regex ($4 still had backticks at match time). The CC silently never fired — no one noticed because archive-manifests for m9-01..m9-10 had stale SHAs but no one compared them.
subject.fix: Fixed CC#4 to strip backticks from BOTH $3 (path) and $4 (sha), trim whitespace, then match. Added exclusion for the self-reference row (a file cannot list its own current SHA because writing the SHA changes the file). Regenerated 54 stale SHAs.

subject.gap: CC#5 (cycles/index.md Total cycles consistency) regex was '^\| (m6 |m[7-9])' which matched all m6/m7/m8 milestone rows (16 extra rows). The CC was silently off-by-16 since the m6/m7/m8 rows were added to cycles/index.md.
subject.fix: Fixed CC#5 to match only m9-* rows, which is what Total cycles represents. After fix: actual=65, declared=65 (was actual=81, declared=65).

subject.gap: CC#48 meta-check only auto-executes python CCs. The 7 bash CCs (CC#1, #4, #5, #6, #46, #53) were validated manually only — silent drift could go unnoticed between sessions.
subject.fix: Added CC#54 (bash, sibling of CC#48) that aggregates drift across all 7 bash CCs. Refactored check_vault_drift.sh to invoke both meta-checks. Both are required for full coverage.
